clue.text: 7 of almost rotten quartz

indicators.note: almost means the word for rotten loses its final letter, stopping just short

parts.note: rotten means bad
quartz is crystalline silica, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: A geologist describes a sample of decaying quartz.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 points to 7-down, a great church; 'almost' trims the last letter of the word for rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often given special status by the Pope, so it is an example of the kind of building at 7-down.

clue.text: Enthusiastic male lead in unknown writer's tragedy

indicators.note: in tells us the enthusiastic word plus the male's lead go inside the unknown writer

parts.note: an unknown writer is Anon, short for anonymous
game means willing or enthusiastic, as in game for anything

indicators.note: lead means the leading, first letter of male

explanation.surface: An eager leading man stars in a tragedy by an anonymous playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon is the tragedy by Aeschylus, first play of the Oresteia trilogy, named after the Greek king murdered on his return from Troy.

clue.text: One competed among climbers

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: set among climbing plants, matching an adjective

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
competed means vied

explanation.surface: A single entrant took part in a contest between mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' suggests mountaineers, but here it means climbing plants such as ivy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ivied is overgrown with ivy, so it sits among climbing plants.

clue.text: Wish to move long distances over a year

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the longing word on top of the year

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it
feet are units of distance

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to travel far afield for twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long distances' reads as one phrase but splits: 'long' is a verb, 'distances' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Having itchy feet is an idiom for restlessness, a strong urge to travel or move on.

clue.text: He asks for a quiet position with very little responsibility

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction meaning quiet
a plié is a ballet position, knees bent

indicators.note: very little of the word responsibility means only its first letter

explanation.surface: A job hunter seeks an undemanding post with hardly any duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' looks like a job, but it is the ballet plié.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies is one who asks for something, such as a post, so the agent noun fits a man asking.

clue.text: Withdraw note about American English

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A memo about American English is pulled back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recuse oneself is to withdraw from a case, as a judge does over a conflict of interest.

clue.text: 7 dwarves had weightless violins?

indicators.note: weightless means without ST, stone, a British unit of weight

parts.note: the strings of an orchestra are its violins and other bowed instruments

explanation.surface: Seven little men played light, featherweight fiddles.
explanation.walkthrough: In Tolkien's verse, seven rings were made for the Dwarf-lords. ST is stone, a weight of 14 pounds still used in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's Rings of Power included seven given to the dwarves, so these are what the dwarves possessed.

clue.text: Cat gets rid of fish in four-sided place of worship

indicators.note: gets rid of says the fish is removed from the word for four-sided

parts.note: a tetrahedral solid has four faces
a tetra is a small tropical aquarium fish

explanation.surface: A cat disposes of fish inside a square chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four-sided' suggests square, but the solid with four faces is the tetrahedron.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese's principal church, the seat of its bishop, is a large place of worship.

clue.text: Film Victor watched outside

indicators.note: outside puts the word for watched around the letter for Victor

parts.note: watched means seen
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Victor was observed watching from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Se7en is David Fincher's 1995 thriller built around the deadly sins.

clue.text: Mother gets money back for starch

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: back says the word for money is read in reverse

parts.note: coin means money

explanation.surface: Mum gets her cash returned for buying laundry starch.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc, or cassava, is the root crop processed into tapioca, a starch.

clue.text: Cruel joke I see breaking restraint

parts.note: a pun is a play-on-words joke

indicators.note: breaking says the letter for see splits the restraint

parts.note: a tie is something that restrains
V is vide, Latin for see, as in cross-references

explanation.surface: A cruel gag that I witness snapping someone's bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Punitive measures are harsh and punishing, so a severe or cruel penalty is punitive.

clue.text: Swirling sand yields bad 7

indicators.note: swirling sand is churned about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Shifting sand produces seven dreadful things.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 7 is simply the number seven: the seven bad things are the sins.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven deadly sins are the wrongs of Christian teaching, pride, greed, lust and the rest, thus a bad seven.

clue.text: Times reflected in odd parts of San Jose

indicators.note: reflected in means the chosen letters are mirrored, read backwards
odd parts are the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of San Jose

explanation.surface: Times are mirrored in strange districts of San Jose.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of SAN JOSE are SNOE, turned to EONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are vast ages, periods of time.

clue.text: Suddenly stop Poles hiding French evidence of disease

indicators.note: hiding says the poles cover up and take the place of the French

parts.note: to freeze is to stop suddenly
S and N are the south and north poles

explanation.surface: Polish people abruptly stop concealing French signs of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people; here it is the compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a symptom, a sign of illness such as a cold.

clue.text: Online reader has a line about votes

definitions.note: a phrase working as an adjective, describing what concerns votes

parts.note: E for electronic, as in e-mail, stands for online
a lector reads lessons in church

explanation.surface: An e-reader has a line on the election.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral matters concern elections and voting, so electoral means relating to votes.

clue.text: Adult teacher, back in class, took a chance

indicators.note: in puts the adult and the reversed teacher inside the class

parts.note: rank means class or grade
A is the film-classification letter for adult

indicators.note: back says the word for teacher is read from right to left

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A grown-up teacher returns to the classroom and gambles.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a risk is to expose oneself to danger, a phrase for gambling on an outcome.

clue.text: Mark swallows last bit of cheddar cheese in 7

indicators.note: swallows means the word for mark takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to note is to mark

indicators.note: last bit of means the final letter of cheddar

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark gulps down the end of the cheddar and another cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 points to 7-down, a great church; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame de Paris is the great Gothic church of Paris, one famous instance of the kind at 7-down.

clue.text: Senior policeman grasses up George Clooney, for one

parts.note: a super is a police superintendent

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for grasses is read bottom to top

parts.note: to grass on someone is to rat, to inform

explanation.surface: A senior police officer informs on a Hollywood actor.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a grass is an informer and to grass is to inform, so 'grasses' gives RATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clooney is a hugely famous film actor, an example of a celebrity of the highest rank.

clue.text: Less than 2 went round swimming hazard

parts.note: under means less than

indicators.note: went round means the letters of the number are spun into another order

parts.note: the numeral 2 gives the word two

explanation.surface: Fewer than two people went round a danger in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' looks like a cross-reference to 2-down, but it is just the number two.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a current flowing beneath the surface, away from the shore, which can drag swimmers out.

clue.text: Would red snow melting be one of these 7?

indicators.note: melting snow loses its form, so these letters flow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: might coloured snow thawing count as a marvel of the world?
explanation.walkthrough: Here 7 is the number seven: the seven marvels of the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World include the Pyramids and the Colossus of Rhodes, marvels of building.

clue.text: These blooming sheep ate fruit without me!

definitions.note: these blooming things, a plural noun phrase for flowers

indicators.note: ate says the sheep take the trimmed fruit inside them

parts.note: tups are rams

indicators.note: without says the letters of me are removed from the fruit

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
the word me is dropped as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry: these confounded sheep ate the fruit and left me none!
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' reads as a mild British oath, but here it means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips are spring flowers, so they are things in bloom.

clue.text: Sweden very popular? Go!

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
hot means very popular, in demand

explanation.surface: A question about whether Sweden is a fashionable travel choice, then an urge to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is an attempt or turn, as in have a go.

clue.text: Roman 7 sick in quiet retreat

indicators.note: in places the sick word inside the reversed quiet
retreat means the word for quiet goes backwards

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Seven Romans fall ill in a peaceful hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 7 is the number seven: Rome's seven hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome was built on seven hills, among them the Palatine and Capitoline.

clue.text: Easily run and hide 7

parts.note: a canter is an easy gallop, a gentle run
to bury is to hide

explanation.surface: Instructions to jog gently away and conceal something.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 points to 7-down, a great church; Canterbury's is the mother church of English Anglicans.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury, in Kent, England, is named for its famous church, which is often called simply by the city's name.

clue.text: Naive people missing in no small change abroad

indicators.note: missing says the letters of in no are taken away

parts.note: innocents are naive, guileless people
these two words are dropped as written

explanation.surface: Gullible tourists overseas have hardly any loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cents are small coins in the US, euro and other foreign currencies, hence small change abroad.

clue.text: Airship this person's used to break British record

indicators.note: to break means the speaker's contraction splits the record open

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
this person is, from the speaker's view, I am, shortened

explanation.surface: A setter boasts about using an airship to set a new British record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' sounds like a sporting record; here it is a vinyl LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, a gas-filled craft without an internal frame.

clue.text: Look right through barrier at site of Brunelleschi's 7

indicators.note: through means the look and the right go within the barrier

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A tourist peers through railings at a Renaissance architect's masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 points to 7-down; Brunelleschi designed the dome of its great church.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence's Duomo, Santa Maria del Fiore, is crowned by the dome Brunelleschi designed, so the city is its location.

clue.text: Fly worried about going through

indicators.note: about says the word for worried is placed around the route word

parts.note: ate means worried, as in what's eating you
via means going through, by way of

explanation.surface: A nervous flyer frets about passing through turbulence.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot or fly an aircraft.

clue.text: Hands round singular songs

indicators.note: round says the hands are wrapped about the singular letter

parts.note: palms are the insides of the hands, standing for them
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Hands are clapped around some exceptional tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms are sacred songs, the hymns of the biblical Book of Psalms.

clue.text: 7 Ephesian martyrs which are found under railway lines

definitions.meaning: the legendary Christian youths walled in a cave at Ephesus who woke centuries later

definitions.text: which are found under railway lines
definitions.meaning: the British word for the wooden or concrete beams beneath the rails, called ties in America

explanation.surface: Seven early saints of Ephesus somehow turn up beneath a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: Railway beams are known by this name in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend tells of seven youths who slept for centuries, and the British railway term names the beams supporting the track.
